cases.label: support
cases.claim: The occupations were classified into two categories: gender-specific and gender-neutral occupations.
cases.quote: Then, we classified the occupations into 2 categories - gender-specific occupation and gender-neutral occupations.
cases.rationale: The source explicitly gives two occupation categories and names both.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The occupations were classified into three categories.
cases.quote: Then, we classified the occupations into 2 categories - gender-specific occupation and gender-neutral occupations.
cases.rationale: The asserted total of three categories conflicts with the stated total of two.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: Three independent human annotators assigned the occupation categories.
cases.quote: These are used in the algorithm for bias checking which will be explained in the next sub-section.
cases.missing: The paragraph does not identify the number or independence of human annotators assigning these categories.
cases.rationale: A source list and category definition do not establish who assigned labels or how many annotators participated.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: Tennis-Data covers the majority of men's matches from 2000 to 2015.
cases.quote: a dataset provided by Tennis-Data, which covers the majority of the matches played on the men's side from 2000-2015 and on the women's side from 2007-2015.
cases.rationale: The source binds the majority coverage and 2000-2015 interval specifically to men's matches.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The stated Tennis-Data coverage period for women's matches starts in 2000.
cases.quote: on the women's side from 2007-2015.
cases.rationale: The stated start year for women's matches is 2007, whereas 2000 belongs to the men's interval.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The study's selected interview dataset contains 50000 transcripts.
cases.quote: For our study, we take post- game interviews for tennis singles matches played between Jan, 2000 to Oct 18, 2015.
cases.missing: The total number of selected interview transcripts is not reported in this paragraph.
cases.rationale: The interview selection interval is supplied, but it does not determine the transcript count.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: The DEX model achieved 91.00% accuracy on APPA-REAL.
cases.quote: We again follow Merler et al. BIBREF18 and employ a DEX model to annotate the gender of an individual. When tested on APPA-REAL, with enhanced annotations provided by BIBREF21 , the model achieves an accuracy of 91.00%
cases.rationale: The adjacent sentences bind the model, APPA-REAL test condition, accuracy metric and exact value.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The DEX model achieved 81.00% accuracy on APPA-REAL.
cases.quote: When tested on APPA-REAL, with enhanced annotations provided by BIBREF21 , the model achieves an accuracy of 91.00%
cases.rationale: For the same model, metric and test condition, the reported value is 91.00%, not 81.00%.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The DEX model achieved 95.00% recall on APPA-REAL.
cases.quote: When tested on APPA-REAL, with enhanced annotations provided by BIBREF21 , the model achieves an accuracy of 91.00%
cases.missing: Recall on APPA-REAL is not reported; the stated accuracy does not determine recall.
cases.rationale: The paragraph reports accuracy and uneven error distribution, but no recall value.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: The Mboshi5K corpus was used as a test set for all reported experiments.
cases.quote: We used the Mboshi5K corpus BIBREF13 as a test set for all the experiments reported here.
cases.rationale: The test-set role and coverage of every reported experiment are stated explicitly.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The Mboshi5K corpus was not used as a test set in any reported experiment.
cases.quote: We used the Mboshi5K corpus BIBREF13 as a test set for all the experiments reported here.
cases.rationale: The denial of any test-set use is refuted by the explicit statement that all reported experiments used this test set.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The Mboshi5K corpus contains 400 hours of speech.
cases.quote: The corpus is multilingual (5130 Mboshi speech utterances aligned to French text)
cases.missing: The total speech duration in hours is not stated; the utterance count does not determine duration.
cases.rationale: The paragraph gives an utterance count and alignment language but no duration measurement.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: The char-lstm model and the word model have identical LAS results for Hindi and Urdu.
cases.quote: the char-lstm model outperforms the word model on LAS for all languages except Hindi and Urdu for which the results are identical.
cases.rationale: Hindi and Urdu are the explicit exceptions for which LAS results are identical.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The char-lstm model outperforms the word model on LAS for every language.
cases.quote: the char-lstm model outperforms the word model on LAS for all languages except Hindi and Urdu for which the results are identical.
cases.rationale: A universal strict improvement is refuted by the two named languages with identical results.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The char-lstm model uses fewer parameters than char-cnn.
cases.quote: the char-lstm generally obtains the best parsing accuracy, closely followed by char-cnn.
cases.missing: Parameter counts or a parameter-count comparison between char-lstm and char-cnn are not provided.
cases.rationale: The source compares parsing accuracy, which does not establish a parameter-count ordering.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: The satirical corpus consists of 9159 headlines published by The Onion.
cases.quote: Our satirical corpus consists of 9,159 headlines published by the wellknown satirical newspaper The Onion
cases.rationale: The source identifies both the exact headline count and The Onion as the satirical source.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The serious corpus consists of 9159 headlines.
cases.quote: our serious corpus, of 9,000 headlines drawn from 9 major news websites.
cases.rationale: The serious corpus has 9000 headlines; 9159 is the count for the distinct satirical corpus.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The satirical corpus contains 20000 word tokens.
cases.quote: Our satirical corpus consists of 9,159 headlines published by the wellknown satirical newspaper The Onion
cases.missing: The word-token count is not supplied; a headline count cannot establish a word-token count.
cases.rationale: The paragraph reports headlines and news sources, not the lengths or token counts of headlines.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: The Raw Text column was entered by a physician.
cases.quote: Each CSV file contains a "Raw Text" column entered by a physician
cases.rationale: The source directly binds the Raw Text column to a physician as its author.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: The training set did not contain any death certificates.
cases.quote: This training set contained 125383 death certificates.
cases.rationale: The explicit positive count refutes the claim of no death certificates.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The training set contains exactly 60000 death certificates for 2014.
cases.quote: Three CSV files (AlignedCauses) were provided by task organizers containing annotated death certificates for different periods : 2006 to 2012, 2013 and 2014. This training set contained 125383 death certificates.
cases.missing: The total is reported, but the number of certificates specifically for 2014 is not supplied.
cases.rationale: A total across three periods does not establish the count for the 2014 subset.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: All trailing sarcasm or emotion hashtags were removed from the data before training and testing.
cases.quote: All trailing “#sarcasm” or emotion hashtags were removed from the data before training and testing
cases.rationale: The source explicitly states removal of all such trailing hashtags before training and testing.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: Trailing sarcasm or emotion hashtags were retained in the data during training and testing.
cases.quote: All trailing “#sarcasm” or emotion hashtags were removed from the data before training and testing
cases.rationale: Retaining these hashtags during training/testing conflicts with removing all of them beforehand.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: Removing trailing hashtags increased test accuracy by five percentage points.
cases.quote: All trailing “#sarcasm” or emotion hashtags were removed from the data before training and testing
cases.missing: No test-accuracy measurement or ablation estimating the effect of hashtag removal is reported in this paragraph.
cases.rationale: A preprocessing description alone does not establish a quantified accuracy improvement.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: Entities do not overlap across the training, validation and testing splits.
cases.quote: We use 70% of examples for training, 20% for validation, and 10% for testing according to a stratified split. As we expect to encounter novel and unknown entities in the wild, we ensure that entities do not overlap across splits and that we only test on unseen entities.
cases.rationale: The source names the three splits and explicitly states that entities do not overlap across them.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: Some entities occur in both the training and testing splits.
cases.quote: we ensure that entities do not overlap across splits and that we only test on unseen entities.
cases.rationale: The existence of a shared training/test entity conflicts with the explicit non-overlap policy.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The dataset contains texts in six languages.
cases.quote: The final dataset consists of 32,227 pairs of news articles and topics annotated with their stance.
cases.missing: The paragraph does not state the languages or the number of languages in the dataset.
cases.rationale: Article/topic counts, stance percentages and split sizes do not determine the number of languages.

cases.label: support
cases.claim: The tested active learning strategies did not work well with the CNN.
cases.quote: However, all the active learning strategies we tested do not work well with deep learning model (i.e., CNN) or deep learning-based ensemble classifier.
cases.rationale: The statement explicitly includes the CNN in the models for which all tested active learning strategies did not work well.

cases.label: contradict
cases.claim: All tested active learning strategies worked well with the CNN.
cases.quote: However, all the active learning strategies we tested do not work well with deep learning model (i.e., CNN) or deep learning-based ensemble classifier.
cases.rationale: The asserted universal success is the opposite of the reported result for the same strategies and CNN.

cases.label: not_enough_info
cases.claim: The CNN achieved an accuracy of 90%.
cases.quote: However, all the active learning strategies we tested do not work well with deep learning model (i.e., CNN) or deep learning-based ensemble classifier.
cases.missing: The paragraph does not provide a numerical CNN accuracy.
cases.rationale: A qualitative statement about active learning suitability does not determine a CNN accuracy value.
